layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branches can be compared.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Aryan and *Iranian.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Indo-Iranian. Branch of *Indo-European divided in turn into *Indo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Indonesian. See Malay-Indonesian.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: induction. Process of reasoning which moves from the particular to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the general. E.g. from a series of observations of individual professors,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: all of whom work very hard, one might draw the inductive inference

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that all professors work very hard.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Opp. deduction: see also abduction.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inessive. *Case whose basic role is to indicate position within

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: something: thus, schematically, I-sit study-ınEss 'I am sitting in a study'

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: INF = infinitive.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: infection. Older term for the influence of one vowel on another, e.g.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in *metaphony or *vowel harmony.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: infectum. Term in Latin grammar for forms of a verb that are not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: marked as *perfect (2). E.g. Latin regit ‘rules' or regebat ‘was ruling' are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forms of, and based on the stem (reg-) of, the infectum; rexit ‘ruled, has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ruled' and rexerat ‘had ruled', based on the stem rex-, are corresponding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forms of the perfectum'.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conditions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: infelicitous. (Speech act) not meeting the required *felicity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inference

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inference. Any conclusion drawn from a set of propositions, from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: something someone has said, and so on. This includes things that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: follow logically: cf. implication, entailment. It also includes things

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that, while not following logically, are implied, in an ordinary sense,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: e.g. in a specific context: cf. e.g. conversational implicature.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inferential. (Particle, inflection) indicating that what is said is based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on inference and not on direct observation. E.g. schematically, They

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: INFERENTIAL are indoors ‘They must be indoors' (because their door is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: open, because they are not visible outside, and so on). Opposed to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other *evidential elements.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: English, the 'bare infinitive' do in I made him do it, and the infinitive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: made and forced, both him do it and him to do it.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: infinitive (ine). A non-*finite form of a verb characteristically used in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: clauses and in other constructions subordinate to another verb: e.g., in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with to, as it is usually described, in I forced him to do it. An infinitive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: clause, or infinitival clause, is one whose verb is in the infinitive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: form: thus in these examples, if clause boundaries are established after

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Originally of forms in e.g. Latin that also regularly headed noun

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phrases: thus, more marginally in English, To buy caviar is expensive.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: position, an infix -m-.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: infix. An *affix or *bound (1) morpheme which is inserted within

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: another form. Thus in Latin rumpo 'I break' the root is rup-: cf. rup-t-us

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'broken'. The stem rump- then consists of the root with, in included

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of one.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Infixation is the process of inserting an infix; a form is infixal if,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: like rump-, it is formed with an infix or, like -m-, it is in the position

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: INFL l'inful]. Name for the verbal inflection of a clause in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *Government and Binding Theory, later generalized as *I.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inflecting. (Language, formation) in which words distinguish

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: grammatical categories whose realizations cannot or cannot easily be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: separated. E.g. in Russian, nouns distinguish case and number; but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a.specific case and a specific number are never realized by distinct

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: endings. Likewise verbs distinguish e.g. a perfective from an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imperfective, commonly realized by a variation within their stems.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: century.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Opp. agglutinating, isolating, in a typology dating from the 19th

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inflection. Any form or change of form which distinguishes different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: grammatical forms of the same lexical unit. E.g. plural books is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distinguished from singular book by the inflection -s, which is by that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: token a plural inflection.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The term originally meant ‘modification' (lit. 'bending'): thus book is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modified, by the addition of -s, to books.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: -ing form

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inflectional class. A class of words or morphemes which have the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: same inflection or inflections. Thus sing is of the same inflectional class

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as sink or drink: as sing is distinguished from sang and sung, so sink is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distinguished from sank and sunk, and drink from drank and drunk.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Major inflectional classes are often described as *conjugations (of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: verbs) or *declensions (of nouns).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inflectional morphology. Branch of *morphology concerned with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *inflections: hence especially with both the semantic and the formal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure of *paradigms. An inflectional affix is similarly an affix

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: described as an inflection, a process by which e.g. such an affix is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: added is an inflectional formation, and so on.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Opp. derivational morphology. But the distinction has often been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenged, e.g. in *Lexical Morphology.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: informant. Any speaker of a language acting as a source for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: statements that a linguist makes about it. For their own language,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: linguists are often their own informants; in investigating one that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: they do not know or that is not theirs, they may work regularly with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a single native speaker or group of speakers.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ‘informer'.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Sometimes replaced by 'consultant' or 'language consultant',

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: especially in the USA, where informant' has developed the sense of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'informationally encapsulated'. See modular.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vs. *comment, *focus, etc.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information structure. The structure of a sentence or larger unit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: viewed as a means of communicating information to an addressee.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Described in terms of *given vs. new, *theme (1) vs. *rheme, *topic (2)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information theory. Mathematical theory developed in the 1950s

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in which the quantity of 'information' carried by a channel of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: communication is defined in terms of the probability with which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specific units may be transmitted. Suppose that messages may consist

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of any letter of the alphabet in any order: then the probability with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which at any stage in the sequence any particular letter will be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transmitted is constant. But suppose instead that messages consist of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: written words in English: then after e.g. initial f the probability that t

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or another f will follow is very low, that u will follow is relatively high,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that r or a will follow even higher. In the second case the quantity of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'information' carried by the channel would be less.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Important in linguistics as a basis for one measure of *redundancy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: -ing form. A verb form in English such as sleeping in those sleeping, We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were sleeping, I like sleeping, Sleeping was impossible. Often so called because

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: no term inherited from the grammatical tradition, such as *present

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: participle or *gerund, is appropriate to all these uses.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ingressive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ingressive. (Air stream or *airstream mechanism) in which the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: direction of flow is inwards. Opp. egressive: for specific mechanisms see

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: click, implosive.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ingvaeonic = Anglo-Frisian.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inherent feature. One which characterizes a word, etc. in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lexicon as opposed to one assigned to it by a specific construction. E.g

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in German a noun is inherently masculine, feminine, or neuter; in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specific constructions it will be contingently singular or plural, or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nominative singular, accusative singular, and so on.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inheritance. Transfer of properties under an operation. E.g. inquiry is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a noun derived from inquire, by an operation under which it inherits

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the property of taking a prepositional phrase with into: They inquired

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [into his expenses], likewise their inquiry [into his expenses]. Also of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: copying of features from a higher to a lower level of constituency. E.g.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a sentence is passive; therefore a verb phrase and a verb within it are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also passive. For this second sense cf. percolation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: initial phrase marker. Term in *transformational grammar for a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phrase structure tree derived by rules of a *base component only,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is then subject to transformations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: initial symbol. See rewrite rule.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Initial Teaching Alphabet. A way of writing English proposed as a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compromise between a phonetic transcription and the conventional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spelling; devised by J. Pitman and promoted in several schools in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Britain in the 1960s and 1970s on the theory that children would

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learn the spelling more easily if they learned this system first.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: initiator. Used of whatever initiates a flow of air in the production

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of speech. Thus in the pulmonic *airstream mechanism an airflow is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: initiated by the organs that control breathing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: injunctive. Term in *Indo-European linguistics for the use of forms

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based on the stem of the indicative in orders and prohibitions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Attested mainly in *Indo-Iranian.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'innate'. Usual in linguistics since the 1960s in the loose sense of ‘in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: part at least determined by genetic inheritance'. Hence, in particular,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the 'innateness hypothesis', with reference to Chomsky's theory of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *universal grammar.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inner form. See Humboldt.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: innovation. Any change by which a language diverges from others

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: historically related to it. E.g. the order of words in Clearly I have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lost represents an innovation in English as compared with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intensifying

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *verb-second order of Old English and other Germanic languages.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: When two members of a family share an innovation, that is prima

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: facie evidence that they are more closely related than either is to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: others.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in pausa. At the end of, or before a break in, an utterance. E.g., in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: many forms of English, a word like beer ends in [ıə] before a consonant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or 'in pausa', but has a *linking [r] before a vowel.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instantaneous release. Chomsky and Halle's term in *SPE for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rapid release of a *stop consonant, in which the resulting flow of air

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is not audibly turbulent. Hence a feature distinguishing e.g. [p} or [t]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from *affricates such as German pf or tsch [tf]. Opp. delayed release.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: institutionalized = established.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instrument used for some purpose. Thus with a fork has an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fork to dig it.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instrumental (1). *Case or *case role of elements indicating an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instrumental role in I dug it with a fork; also, in accounts following

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that of *Case Grammar, a fork in A fork would dig it easily or I used a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: practical end. Cf. conative.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instrumental (2). (*Function of language) in achieving some

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and fruitful.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instrumentalism. Philosophical theory, developed in the late 19th

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: century by J. Dewey, which holds that beliefs, hypotheses, etc. are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instruments with which we engage with the world in which we live,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and are therefore justified simply to the extent that they are successful

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which are.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: integration. Process by which a word, etc. borrowed from another

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language becomes part of the native system. Thus the [3l of rouge or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mirage, both in origin *loan words from French, is not fully integrated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into English phonology, since its distribution, within the syllable and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in relation to the vowels that it follows, is more restricted than that of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [S] (sh) and others to which it is most directly opposed. Likewise the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: words as wholes are not fully integrated, unlike words in [∫| such as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: push or brush, themselves much earlier borrowings from French,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intensifying. (Word, intonation, inflection) which in any way adds

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: emphasis to a sentence or some element within it. Thus, schematically,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: He did-ıNTENs it might mean ‘He really did it'.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'Intensifier' is used by Quirk et al., *CGE, of a class of adverbial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: elements (in their terms a class of *subjuncts) with an intensifying role

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that is either positive or negative. The positive ones are amplifiers and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: include, as amplifiers of the strongest degree, maximizers such as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: completely or utterly; the negative are downtoners and include, at the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other end of a scale, minimizers such as hardly or scarcely

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intension

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intension. The properties that define a word or concept. An

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intensional definition of a class will correspondingly specify the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properties that something must have to be a member of it. Opp.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extension, extensional.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: An intensional logic is one in which the validity of arguments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: depends on identity or difference in intension, opposed again to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extension.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: measured in decibels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intensity. The physical correlate of perceived loudness, usually

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intensive. (Verb) which takes a *predicative adjective or noun

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phrase: e.g. those of She is angry, He seemed a nice man. Also of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pattern of *complementation associated with it: thus angry and a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nice man are described as 'intensive complements'.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cf. copular, predicative, both of which are used more widely.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of language.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interchangeability. The property of language by which the roles

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of speaker and addressee are interchangeable. Thus any sentence one

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: might utter one would also understand if said by someone else and, in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: principle, vice versa. Defined as one of the proposed *design features

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interdental. (Consonant) articulated with the tip of the tongue

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: protruded between the teeth: e.g. in one pronunciation of (th) [θ] in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interference. The influence that knowledge of one language has on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the way one speaks another: e.g. in the speech of bilinguals, or as a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cause of errors by someone learning a new language.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interfix. A morphological element serving simply as a link between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other elements. E.g. -i- in Latin particeps 'participant' or aquifolia 'holly',

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seen as linking two members of a compound (part-i-ceps, aqu-i-folia).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interjection. Traditionally of forms that express 'states of mind' and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: do not enter into specific syntactic relations with other words: e.g.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Wow, Yuk, Phew. Some, such as phew [φ:|, are also idiophones, with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phonetic features peculiar to them.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A *part of speech in ancient Roman accounts of Latin. Extended by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some recent writers to a larger and more indeterminate category of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which the traditional interjections are only part.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interlanguage. 1. A language, or an artificial system like a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language, used as an intermediary, e.g. in translation, between two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: others. 2. A system of rules said to develop, in the mind of someone

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning a foreign language, which is intermediate between that of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their native language and that of the one being learned.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inter-level. A *level of description defined as a link between two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: others: e.g. phonology defined, as by Halliday in the early 1960s, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one linking grammar and phonetics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: International Phonetic Alphabet

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: internal argument. One not external to a *predicate (1) or *verb

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phrase: thus specifically an object as opposed to a subject.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: internal causes. Causes of change seen as internal to a language or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the community that speaks it. Thus an internal cause of sound

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: change might be an increase in the *coarticulation of adjacent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consonants, or the pressure to maintain an audible difference

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between vowels; an external cause might be contact with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: system of a neighbouring language.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: internal history. The history of changes in the structure of a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language, as opposed to its *external history. E.g. it is part of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: wrote in it.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: internal history of English that rules of word order changed over the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: early Middle Ages; part of its external history that e.g. Shakespeare

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *I-language.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'internalize'. Used by Chomsky from the late 1950s for the process of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constructing representations in the mind. Thus, in learning a native

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language, a child was seen as ‘internalizing' its grammar. Hence, in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Chomsky's terminology in the 1980s, 'internalized language' or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: internal reconstruction. The attempted *reconstruction of earlier

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stages of a language on the evidence of that language alone. Thus there

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are alternations in English between e.g. [aı] and [1]: wise vs. wisdom, vice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vs. vicious, etc. On that evidence alone, one might argue, first, that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: either or both vowels must show the effect of sound change, and,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: secondly, that the most plausible changes would derive wis(e) and vic(e)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from reconstructed *[wi:z], *[vi:s].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: internal sandhi. Processes of phonological modification (*sandhi)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found within words, at or across the boundaries of roots or affixes.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: within larger units.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: internal syntax. The relations, rules, etc. that apply within a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: syntactic unit, as opposed to those into which it enters, as a whole,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diplomacy, etc.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: international language. One used internationally; specifically, one

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recognized officially as a language of international meetings,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vowel system.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: International Phonetic Alphabet. The system of phonetic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transcription developed and promoted by the *International Phonetic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Association. Consonants are classified by *place and *manner of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: articulation, with boxes in the resulting grid filled, where there is no

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: appropriate letter in the Roman alphabet, with special letters partly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resembling them. *Secondary articulations, and some manners of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: articulation not distinguished by the Roman alphabet, are shown by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diacritics. The transcription of vowels is according to the *cardinal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: International Phonetic Association

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The increasing adoption of this system is without doubt one of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: most important practical achievements oflinguistics in the 20th

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: century.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: International Phonetic Association. Society founded in France in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1886 by Passy and called by this name since 1897. Its original aim was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to promote the use of phonetic script in teaching modern European

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: languages, and its journal, Le Maître Phonétique ('The Phonetic Teacher'),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: published articles in the *International Phonetic Alphabet which it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: devised. In the course of the 20th century its interests have become

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increasingly academic, with its centre shifted to Britain. Its present

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: journal, the Journal of the International Phonetic Association, replaced Le

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Maître Phonétique in 1970.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Passy and his pupil (Daniel) Jones were leading figures for much of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its history.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the *expressive (affective, emotive) function.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interpersonal. (Meaning, *function of language) in developing and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maintaining social relations between people. Alternatively, that is said

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to be the social function: the interpersonal then includes both that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interpretant. Peirce's term for the effect that a sign has on someone

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: who interprets or understands it. Hence *pragmatics was originally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: defined by the relation that signs have to interpretants.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some system of *formal semantics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interpreted. (Logical calculus, etc.) assigned an interpretation in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'Interpretive Semantics'. Applied in the early 1970s to any model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of *transformational grammar in which *semantic representations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of sentences are derived from what are seen as purely formal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: representations of their syntax. The rules by which they were derived

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: had been described by Chomsky in *Aspects as purely interpretive'.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Such models included both the *Standard Theory of Aspects and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modifications of it leading to the *Extended Standard Theory.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Opp. Generative Semantics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are they taking us?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interrogative. (Construction, etc.) whose primary role is in asking

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: questions: e.g. that of Is he here? as distinguished from the *declarative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: He is here. An interrogative particle or interrogative inflection is one

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which marks an interrogative: e.g. in the equivalent sentence in Latin,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a *clitic -ne (adestne? 'be-present-3SG-INTERRoG'). An interrogative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pronoun, adverb, etc. is one that represents a focus of questioning:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: e.g. who or what in Who did this?, What have they done?; where in Where

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The terms ‘question' and 'interrogative' are often interchanged.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: E.g. Is he here? is a question or is an interrogative sentence or ‘an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interrogative'. But a distinction can and sometimes must be made.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intransitivizer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Thus Can't you shut up? has the construction of an interrogative, but its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: usual role would not be as a question but as a request or order. Cf.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: declarative; imperative.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interrogative tag. A *tag in the form of an *interrogative: e.g. has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: he? in He hasn't left, has he?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interrupted (consonant) = abrupt.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intersection. Technically of an operation on sets by which the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intersection (or product) of sets A and B is the set of all elements,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: possibly none, which are members of both. Cf. union (1).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intervocalic. Appearing between vowels. E.g. [p} is an intervocalic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consonant in kipper ['kıpə].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intonation. A distinctive pattern of *tones over a stretch of speech in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: principle longer than a word. Thus there is a difference in intonation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between e.g. That's IT ('I'm finished') and That's IT? ('Is that all?’).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A description of intonation usually has three main aspects. First, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: groups. Secondly, a syllable or series of syllables within each will be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of successive pitch phonemes.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relevant stretches of speech must be identified: in that way sentences

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or utterances are divided into successive intonational units or *tone

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: described as nuclear or *tonic: this will be a position of prominence,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: identified e.g. by a rapid change of pitch. Thirdly, a specific pattern of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tones will be distinguished: this might be described as an overall tune

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or *contour (rising, falling, falling and then rising, etc.) or might

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alternatively be divided into a sequence of smaller components, each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with its own pitch level. Descriptions in terms of contours are usual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: e.g. in British treatments; the alternative treatment derives in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particular from American accounts in the 1940s and 1950s, in which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: patterns of intonation were described as *pitch morphemes composed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intonation group = tone group.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intransitive. Construction in which a verb is related to a single noun

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or its equivalent: e.g. that of They vanished. An intransitive verb, or an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intransitive sense of a verb, is one that takes such a construction: e.g.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vanish, or dry with the sense it has in It will dry. Opp. transitive.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: element.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intransitive preposition. A word such as away in He walked away,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seen as a preposition which takes no complement. Traditionally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: classed as an adverb, since, in the ancient account of *parts of speech,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prepositions were defined as preposed to a noun or some other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shattered'.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intransitivizer. Affix, etc. marking a verb as intransitive rather than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transitive. E.g., schematically, Vase shattered-INTRAns 'The vase

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intrinsic allophone

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intrinsic allophone. A variant of a *phoneme which can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: explained by the phonetic context, without invoking a specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phonological rule: e.g. one which is an effect of *coarticulation. Opp.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extrinsic allophone; but the validity of the distinction depends in part

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at least on how the relation between phonetics and phonology is in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: general perceived.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intrinsic ordering. See ordered rules.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intrinsic pitch. The pitch of a vowel in abstraction from the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vibration of the vocal cords. Thus [i] has a higher intrinsic pitch,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in terms of the underlying resonance of the vocal tract, than [a]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intrusive r. See linking r.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feeling that a linguist may have in investigating it. Likewise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'counter-intuitive'.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intuition. Variously of the intuitive grasp that people have or may

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have of the structure of their own language, and of the intuitive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Arctic to Greenland and Labrador.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Inuit. Often = Eskimo. Specifically of a branch of Eskimo within

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *Eskimo-Aleut, spoken from the Norton Sound in Alaska across the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: invariable word. One which does not have two or more forms with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different grammatical meanings. E.g. but or never, as compared e.g.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with woman, which distinguishes singular woman and plural women.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: invariant. Not changing. E.g. in the classic theory of the *phoneme

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the *distinctive features that characterize each unit are invariant; the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: features with which it is realized in different positions or in different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: combinations vary. The aim of phonological analysis is accordingly to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: discover invariants that underlie surface variation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inverse. (Form of verb, affix) indicating, e.g. in Algonquian

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: languages, that of two elements in a clause that differ on some scale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of *empathy, it is the one lower on the scale that is the *agent.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Opp. direct. Thus, if third person forms are lower on the scale than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: first persons, a sentence meaning 'I kissed the sister' will be marked as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: direct: schematically, with the persons marked respectively by a prefix

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and a suffix, 1sT-kissed-DiR-3RD sister. A sentence meaning ‘The sister

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: kissed me' will instead be marked as inverse. Thus, with the persons

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: marked in the same way in the same positions, 1st-kissed-ınv-3RD sister.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inversion. Any operation by which the order x + y is changed to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: y + x. E.g. an interrogative in English (Is he here?) is related to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corresponding declarative (He is here) by inversion of the subject (he)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and a verb (in this case is).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inverted commas. Used variously for things other than individual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forms considered in abstraction, Thus for glosses or translations: e.g.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: irreversible binomial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: French arbre 'tree', Elle vient 'She is coming'. Also for propositions seen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as expressed by sentences: e.g. both French Elle vient and English She

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is coming express the proposition ‘She is coming'’. Also for units

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: represented at a higher level of abstraction: e.g. coming is a form of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: verb 'to come'. Also of a form as uttered on a specific occasion: thus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'She's coming' would represent an utterance of She's coming.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'invisible hand' theory. Model of change in language in which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: change in a given direction emerges, as if directed ‘by an invisible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hand', from the separate behaviour of individual speakers, directed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in itself to strictly individual ends. An application to linguistics by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: R. Keller of an account by Adam Smith in economics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IO = indirect object.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Parameters Theory headed by *I (= INFL).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IP. 1. = Item and Process. 2. A phrase (P) in Chomsky's *Principles and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Association.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IPA = International Phonetic Alphabet, International Phonetic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Iranian. Branch, within *Indo-European, of *Indo-Iranian, first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attested by religious texts in *Avestan and inscriptions in Old Persian

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the reign of Darius I (522-486 Bc). The modern languages are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spoken mainly in a continuous area from eastern Turkey through Iran

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to Afghanistan and Tajikistan: *Persian, *Pashto, *Kurdish, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *Baluchi are in order of size the most important.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: irony. Traditionally of a *figure of speech in which one thing is said

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but the opposite is meant: e.g. 'That's just what I needed!', said as the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tool one is using comes apart in one's hands. Usage in pragmatics or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: linguistics generally tends to reflect this, but others are also current,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in literary studies especially.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Iroquoian. Family of languages spoken or formerly spoken in parts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of eastern North America. The main group were and in part are in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Great Lakes region from Lake Huron eastwards: this includes Mohawk.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Others include Cherokee, displaced to Oklahoma by ethnic cleansing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the 19th century.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in this way.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: irrealis [ırer'a:lis]. (Form of verb) used to refer to something that has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not happened or is unlikely to happen. E.g. had got is ‘an irrealis' in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *remote or unreal conditional if you had got there on time; likewise were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in I was hoping you were in town tomorrow. Especially of past tenses used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: irregular. See regular.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: irreversible binomial. A pair of words in a fixed and parallel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relation: e.g. (It is raining) cats and dogs, not dogs and cats; ( just a few)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: odds and ends, not ends and odds.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: island

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: island. A syntactic unit whose boundaries form a barrier to specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: syntactic relations or processes. For an example see coordinate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure constraint: cf. complex NP constraint, wh-island constraint.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: An island constraint or condition is any such principle by which an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: island is defined.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: isochrony. Principle by which phonological units tend to be equally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spaced in time: e.g. syllables in languages that are *syllable-timed,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stresses in those that are *stress-timed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: isogloss. A line on a map dividing areas whose dialects differ in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some specific respect: e.g. between dialects in which a consonant is in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: principle voiced and those in which the corresponding consonant is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: voiceless, or those in which a certain thing is normally called x and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: those in which it is normally called y.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Major divisions between dialects are characterized by bundles of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: isoglosses, in which many such lines tend to run together.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phonology, characterized by a unique pair of features: e.g. in Spanish,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between trilled [r] (rr) in perro ‘dog' and flapped [r} (r) in pero 'but'.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Distinguished as such from members of a *correlation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: isolated opposition. An opposition, especially in *Prague School

layout_dets.text: theory of *transformational grammar until the mid-1960s, when

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transformations combining separate sentences were rejected in favour

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of rules which derived corresponding structures in a *base

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'key'. 1. Used in studies of intonation for a distinction in an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intonational unit between relatively narrow variation in pitch and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: variation which extends higher: e.g. between l'd be de LiGíted said

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: without emotional involvement and with a relatively low pitch at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the beginning of `LiGh, and the same said enthusiastically, with a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relatively high pitch instead. 2. Also, in the *ethnography of speaking,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the manner (e.g. hurried or calm) in which speech is delivered.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: key word. A word or concept characteristic of the thought of a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particular community in a particular period. E.g. ‘raison' (reason) is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a key word of the French Enlightenment; rigo(u)r' a key word for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: American linguists in the 1940s and 1950s.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Khmer. The national language of Cambodia (also called ‘Cambodian')

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A member of the *Mon-Khmer family, attested from at least the 7th

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: century Ap, originally in a South *Indian script which has evolved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into the present writing system.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Khoisan. Group of languages in southern Africa, spoken mainly in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the Kalahari region in Namibia and Botswana: those, in particular, of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the peoples collectively called Bushman. Two non-Bantu languages of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Tanzania have also been included in it.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kikuyu. *Bantu, spoken in Central Province, Kenya.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: kinesics. The study of meaningful gestures and other body

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: movements in communication. Originally of a treatment modelled on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kurdish

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: American linguistics in the 1950s, with e.g. 'kinemes' as the smallest

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gestural units.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: kinetic tone = contour tone.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: kinship terms. Words identifying the relationship of other members

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of a person's family: e.g. sister or grandson. A kinship system is the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: system of oppositions among such terms in a given language or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: culture.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kiowa-Tanoan. A small family oflanguages in the American South-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: west, primarily in Mexico and Oklahoma. Conjecturally related to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *Uto-Aztecan.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kirghiz. See Turkic.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kiswahili = Swahili.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: koiné. 1. The form of Greek that became general in the eastern

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mediterranean after the conquests of Alexander in the 4th century

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Bc. From a word meaning '(in) common'. 2. Generalized in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sociolinguistics to any varieties of a language that arise historically by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evening out differences among dialects. Thus *standard languages

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: may sometimes develop by a process of 'koinéization'.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Komi. The main *Finno-Ugric language in the region of the Urals;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also called 'Zyryan'. The branch it belongs to is called 'Permic'.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kongo. *Bantu, spoken in Congo, Zaire, and Angola, north and south

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the River Congo from Brazzaville to the sea.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kerala.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Konkani. The southernmost *Indo-Aryan language, historically of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Goa and a surrounding area, but also spoken through emigration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: elsewhere in south India, in parts of the states of Karnataka and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kordofanian. A group of languages centred on the Nuba Mountains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the south of Kordofan province, Sudan.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Korean. Limited historically to the Korean peninsula, and at best

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conjecturally related to any other language. Originally written in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Chinese characters, which are still not wholly supplanted: more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generally, however, and in North Korea especially, in an alphabet

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (see Han'gul) which in its modern form has twenty-four basic letters.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Coast.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kru. Family of languages in the south of Liberia and south-west Ivory

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kurdish. *Iranian language spoken in various countries from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: western Turkey across north-east Iraq to the north-east of the Persian

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Gulf. There is a major division between northern and southern

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dialects, roughly at the level of Mosul.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kwa

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kwa. Group of languages in West Africa, including *Akan in Ghana

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and, in accounts formerly at least accepted, Nigerian languages such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as *Yoruba and *Igbo.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kwakiutl. See Wakashan.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: kymograph. An early instrument, in use in phonetics until the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1960s, which mechanically recorded e.g. muscular movements or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: changes of air pressure by traces on paper.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: L

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: L. See diglossia.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: L,, L₂ = first language, second language. Especially in discussion of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language teaching, where L2 is the 'target language', or language to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be learned.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labelled bracketing. Notation in which the constituents of a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: syntactic or other unit are enclosed in square brackets which are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labelled, by subscripts, for the categories to which they belong. Thus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in npł [tall] [men]], tall is assigned to the category ‘adjective' (A), men to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the category 'noun' (N), and the whole is a constituent assigned to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: class 'noun phrase' (NP).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The labels for categories are variously written before the opening

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: brackets, as here, or after them: [p [tall] [men]]. Occasionally they

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are subscripted to both the opening and the closing brackets:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: NP| [tall], N[men|N |NP.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labial. 1. Cover term for *bilabial and *labiodental. 2. = bilabial in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cases of *double articulation (2). Thus [gb| is a labial velar; {ib| or [d3b]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a labial palatal.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labialized or 'rounded' velars (k", etc.) contrast with non-labialized.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labialization. Lip rounding as a *secondary articulation. E.g. {S] in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shoe is phonetically labialized; in many languages, e.g. in the Caucasus,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: e.g. [f] in fin or [v] in veal.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labiodental. Articulated with the lower lip against the upper teeth:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labiovelar. 1. A velar consonant accompanied by distinctive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *labialization: usually written k", g", and so on. 2. = labial velar.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Labov, William (1927- ). A pioneer in sociolinguistics from the mid-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1960s, whose early work on class-based variation in the speech of New

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: York and elsewhere led the field, both as a model of research and as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the subject of theoretical and other criticism and refinement, into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the 1980s. He has consistently advocated the application both of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: findings of sociolinguistics and of sociolinguistic models of a speech

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: community to the study of change in languages.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: LAD. For 'Language Acquisition Device': posited by Chomsky in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1960s as a device effectively present in the minds of children by which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a *grammar of their native language is constructed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lag. See voice onset time; also progressive assimilation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: LAGB = Linguistics Association of Great Britain.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Lakota

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Lakota. See Siouan.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lambda operator (λ). Logical operator by which an expression

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which denotes a set is derived from one which represents a property,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: etc. by which the set is defined. Thus λx (clever (x))' is a lambda

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: expression denoting the set of all individuals who are clever, derived

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from a predication ‘clever (x)' which includes x as a variable.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The operation is said to ‘abstract on' the variable: hence 'lambda

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: abstraction'. An expression such as ‘λx (clever (x)) (Bill)' (an individual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: what is called 'lambda conversion', to clever (Bill)' (Bill is clever).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Bill is a member of the set of all individuals who are clever) reduces, by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alveolar consonant, such as [t] in tip, is articulated with the blade

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: laminal. Articulated with the *blade of the tongue. A lamino-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: against the ridge behind the upper teeth; a lamino-dental with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: blade against the teeth themselves. Also called 'laminar'.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'landing site'. Informally, in *Government and Binding Theory, of a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: position into which some element is, or can be, moved.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: langage. The phenomenon of language in general: = language (2).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Term from French used especially in opposition to *langue (= language

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1) or *language system) and *parole.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language. 1. A language in the ordinary sense: e.g. English or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Japanese. Opp. dialect, also as in ordinary usage. 2. The phenomenon

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of vocal and written communication among human beings generally,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: again as in ordinary usage. Thus the subject-matter of linguistics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: includes both language as a general property of our species (sense 2)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and particular languages (sense 1).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'Language' in sense 2 is often extended to cover other forms of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: communication; hence, in particular, 'animal language' for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: communicative behaviour in other species. 'A language' in sense 1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is defined more precisely in different ways according to different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: theories. For some it is a *language system underlying the speech

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of a community: thus especially a *langue as defined by Saussure.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Alternatively, it is a system in the mind of an individual: thus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: especially *I-language as defined by Chomsky in the mid-1980s. Others

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have conceived it as the set of sentences potentially observable in a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: speech community: thus especially a definition by Bloomfield in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1920s. Alternatively, it is the set of sentences characterized or to be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: characterized by a *generative grammar: thus Chomsky in the 1950s.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A *formal language is accordingly defined, by extension, in a way that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is taken to apply not only to so-called *natural languages (2), or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: languages in the ordinary sense 1, but also to artificial systems in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: logic, computing, etc.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'language acquisition'. Usually, if not qualified e.g. as 'second

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language acquisition', of the development of language in children.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For 'Language Acquisition Device' see LAD.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'language suicide'

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'language consultant' = informant.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'language death'. The disappearance of a language whose speakers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: progressively switch to using another or others, e.g. of many languages

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in North America once spoken by people whose descendants speak

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only English.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: speakers.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cf. dead language. But a language may become 'dead' in other ways:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by a historical break in identity, as with Latin, or, as with others in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: North America and elsewhere, by physical extermination of their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'language deficit'. See deficit theory.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language faculty. Faculty of the mind, in the traditional sense,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: controlling language. Used by Chomsky in the 1960s: hence the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domain of *universal grammar (2) and of *I-language within a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *modular theory of the mind in general.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language family. See family.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Language for Special Purposes. Any programme directed towards

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the teaching of a foreign language for use in some specific context:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thus English e.g. for air to ground communication with airports.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language isolate. A language that cannot to our knowledge be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assigned to any larger *family. Basque is a classic example.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'language murder'. *Language death represented as the killing off

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of a language by another whose speakers are e.g. politically dominant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: French 'glottophagie' is perhaps less seriously tendentious.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language planning. Any attempt by a government, etc. to favour

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one language, or one form of a language, over another. This includes,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: e.g., the choice of an official language for a country or province; the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: official development of a standard form; the promotion by an academy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or other body of native terms to be used in place of loan words.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language sign. See linguistic sign

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'language specific'. (Rules, etc.) specific to a particular language:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: e.g. rules in English for the position of adverbs (I have often done it, not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: I often have done it) are, in part at least, peculiar to it. Opposed especially

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to principles, etc. that are hypothetically part of *universal grammar,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in that they hold whatever the language.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'language suicide'. Process by which the speech of a community is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assimilated to that of a larger community, to the point at which it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loses its separate identity. Conceived as a form of voluntary 'language

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: death', as opposed to *language murder.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cf. decreolization.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language system

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language system. The system of a specific language at a specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time, seen in abstraction from its history; from its use on specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: occasions and by specific individuals; from other systems of culture,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: knowledge, etc.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The scope and status of language systems have been debated, under

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one name or another, throughout the 20th century. For some they are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at best constructs, to be posited to the extent that they are useful. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: others they are a real object of description, though conceived in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: varying ways. Cf. language.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language universal = linguistic universal.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: langue = language system. French term borrowed from Saussure, for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whom 'la langue' was a social reality (‘fait social') constraining each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: speaker. Opposed in that sense to 'langage' (the phenomenon of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language in general) and to individual speech performance or *parole.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: langue véhiculaire. French term for a language used in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: communication between members of societies whose own languages

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are different: e.g. French itself in much of West and Central Africa.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *Khmer (Cambodian).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Lao. Language of the *Tai family, spoken in the valley of the River

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mekong, in northern Laos and downstream in both Laos and Thailand

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into Cambodia. Official in Laos; the script is derived from that of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Lappish. See Sami.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: laryngeal. 1. = glottal: thus [h} is sometimes called a laryngeal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fricative. 2. One of a set of consonants established in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *reconstruction of an Indo-European *protolanguage to explain,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in particular, what are otherwise aberrant alternations and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correspondences of vowels. The 'laryngeal theory' is the hypothesis,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: now generally accepted, that such consonants existed: they are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presumed to have been *pharyngeal fricatives or others articulated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: towards the back of the vocal tract, but the only direct evidence, found

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: after they had been first proposed, is in *Anatolian.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: laryngealized. Accompanied by *creak: thus a laryngealized vowel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is one produced with creaky voice.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: laryngoscopy. Any of the successive techniques that have been used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to study the action of the *vocal cords.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: words like bottle [bptl] or muddle [madl].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: muscles of the vocal tract. Opp. tense (2).

layout_dets.text: learnability. 1. Identified as a *design feature of language, by which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: any member of our species. 2. Property of *formal languages defined

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by a procedure which is designed to construct a grammar from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: successive sentences presented to it. A language is learnable if, after a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sufficient number of sentences have been presented, a grammar can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constructed which does not have to be amended to cope with others. It

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For sense 2 cf. discovery procedure. The mathematical theory of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learned language ['lə:nıd]. One whose only status is as a language

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taught to an educated élite: e.g. Latin as spoken or written in Europe

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the early Middle Ages. Learned forms or learned formations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are characteristically those perceived by speakers as belonging to or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: derived from a learned language: e.g. English rictus ‘grin' is a learned

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: form transparently from Latin.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'least effort'. See principle of least effort.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 'lect'. Any distinct variety of a language: e.g. a regional dialect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (‘dia-lect'), or one used at a specific social level ('socio-lect’). 'Lectal'

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: depends on and precedes the head noun policy, tightly in turn depends

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on and precedes controlled, and very depends on and precedes tightly.

layout_dets.text: position of the dislocated element. Cf. right dislocation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: length. Phonetic or phonological feature, especially of vowels. E.g. in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Latin the vowel of rosa (nominative singular of the word for rose') was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: short ( (rosal); that of rosū (ablative singular of the same word) was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: long (rosa:|). A phonological distinction may be realized, in part or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entirely, by differences other than physical duration. E.g. the 'long'

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vowels of Dutch, in words like laat 'late' or leeg ‘empty', differ

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: systematically in quality and tongue posture from the short' vowels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For long vs. short syllables see heavy syllable. Phonetically long

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consonants tend to be described as *geminate.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with lower muscular tension; hence traditionally of voiced consonants

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as opposed to voiceless. From Latin lenis ‘gentle, weak'. Opp. fortis: cf.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a phonetic value. Thus, in ancient accounts, the letter (Latin litera) was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
